reason: The immature red cells have the machinery to make haemoglobin from its building materials.
expectation: The cells should produce haemoglobin needed to carry oxygen.

effect: The developing cells matured into red blood cells after receiving the haemoglobin building materials; they can now be paired with oxygen.
reaction: The maturation picture helps connect haemoglobin production with the mature cells.
reason: Red blood cells use haemoglobin to carry oxygen, so pairing them with oxygen directly advances the goal.
expectation: The red blood cells should pick up oxygen.

effect: The red blood cells now carry oxygen, and the description explains how haemoglobin can release it in working tissues. The remaining pieces suggest assembling the plasma next.
reaction: The binding and release explanation makes the oxygen carrier's role clearer.
reason: Plasma water and plasma solutes appear to be the components of the liquid portion of the blood sample.
expectation: They should form plasma for the blood sample.

effect: The water and solutes formed plasma, so the liquid portion is ready to join the blood cells.
reaction: The result was predictable, but it clarified what the plasma contains.
reason: Combining plasma with the oxygen-bearing red blood cells should assemble the main parts of the sample.
expectation: The red blood cells should become suspended in the plasma.

effect: The plasma needed the white cells and platelets first; the automatic combination has added them, leaving the oxygen-bearing red blood cells to complete the sample.
reaction: The required order was unexpected, but the compatibility feedback made the next step clear.
reason: The plasma mixture and oxygen-bearing red blood cells are the remaining components of the blood sample.

choice.combine: Plasma with white cells and platelets

expectation: They should form a blood sample that can carry oxygen.

effect: The final combination completed the blood sample and connected plasma, red cells, white cells and platelets to their roles in blood.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separate components come together, though the final assembly was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to the red blood cells was most worthwhile: the description explained both binding and release, connecting the carrier to the needs of working tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma was straightforward, but the result added little beyond showing that it contains dissolved particles and proteins.

surprise.text: I expected oxygen-bearing red cells to combine directly with plasma, but the game required white cells and platelets first. The feedback automatically made that combination.

arbitrary.text: The required order for adding blood cells felt arbitrary; the descriptions did not explain why white cells and platelets had to join the plasma before red cells.

continue.text: I would choose to continue because I am curious how circulation will bring the oxygen carriers close to the arm's cells. I would hope later combinations make their required order clearer.
